JP/Tokyo.cultural_notes: Formality matters. Bowing depth matters. Business cards with both hands.

slang_era.gen_z: 草 (kusa=lol), ぴえん (pien=sad), エモい (emoi), やばい (yabai=amazing/terrible)
slang_era.millennial: マジで (maji de=seriously), ウケる (ukeru=funny), 推し (oshi=fave)
slang_era.older: ございます forms, しょうがない (shouganai=it can't be helped)

JP/Osaka.cultural_notes: Direct, humorous, food-obsessed. なんでやねん is quintessential.

slang_era.gen_z: めっちゃ (meccha=very), あかんて (akante=no way)
slang_era.millennial: なんでやねん, ほんまに (honmani=really), あかん (akan=no good)
slang_era.older: おおきに (ookini=thank you), あきまへん (akimahen=no good)

VN/Ho Chi Minh City.cultural_notes: Called Saigon by locals. Casual vibe. Coffee culture central.

slang_era.older: Formal pronouns (ông/bà), traditional politeness, indirect speech

FR/Paris.cultural_notes: ALWAYS start with Bonjour. Vous before tu. Effort in French appreciated.

slang_era.gen_z: C'est chaud (intense), la flemme (can't be bothered), sah (fr fr)
slang_era.millennial: kiffer (to love), grave (totally), ouf (crazy, verlan of fou)
slang_era.older: Literary tenses, proper subjunctive, fewer anglicisms

MX/Mexico City.cultural_notes: Extremely friendly. Diminutives everywhere. Güey=dude. Ahorita=soon not now.

slang_era.gen_z: neta (fr fr), nmms (no mames), cringe (English loan)
slang_era.older: Usted more common, formal diminutives, fewer anglicisms

KR/Seoul.cultural_notes: Age hierarchy is everything. Ask age early — determines speech level.

NP/Kathmandu.cultural_notes: Kathmandu Valley — Hindu/Buddhist mix, young urban population, Hindi film influence, English common in educated circles. Namaste (नमस्ते) with hands folded is universal. Write phrases in both Devanagari script and romanized transliteration.

slang_era.gen_z: यार (yaar=friend), छ (chha=is/yes), लु (lu=ok/alright), झैं (jhain=like/similar to), किन गर्छस् (kin garcchas=why do you do this)
slang_era.millennial: हजुर (hajur=yes/respect), ठीक छ (thik chha=ok), क्या हो (kya ho=what's up), मिल्यो (milyo=got it/found it)
slang_era.older: Formal honorifics हजुर, सेवामा (sewama=at your service), indirect speech, classical Nepali terms

ES/Barcelona.cultural_notes: Barcelona locals mix Catalan and Spanish freely. Many signs are in Catalan first. Use 'vale' instead of 'ok'. Greetings may be in Catalan (bon dia, adéu). The local identity is strongly Catalan, not just Spanish.

slang_era.gen_z: tio/tia for everything, quedamos? for hangouts

ES/Madrid.cultural_notes: Madrid Spanish is considered 'standard' but locals use heavy slang. Pronounce 'c' and 'z' as 'th'. Nightlife starts at midnight. Directness is valued.

IT/Rome.cultural_notes: Romans speak with distinctive accent and local expressions. 'Daje' is the quintessential Roman word. Hand gestures are communication. Coffee after 11am is suspicious.

TH/Bangkok.cultural_notes: Thai has 5 tones - getting them wrong changes meaning completely. Add 'ka' (female) or 'krap' (male) to be polite. Never touch someone's head. The wai greeting shows respect.

DE/Berlin.cultural_notes: Berlin German is famously direct and informal. 'Ick' instead of 'ich'. Multicultural slang from Turkish and English. Berliners take pride in being unimpressed.

BR/São Paulo.cultural_notes: São Paulo Portuguese is fast and drops final syllables. 'Mano' (bro) is universal. Everything is 'legal' (cool). The city never sleeps and neither does the slang.

CN/Shanghai.cultural_notes: Shanghainese is a separate dialect from Mandarin but most young people speak Mandarin with Shanghainese flavoring. Business culture is fast-paced. Food is sweeter than northern China.

slang_era.millennial: 牛逼, 佛系, 摸鱼
slang_era.older: 哎呀, 不得了, 厉害

AR/Buenos Aires.cultural_notes: Buenos Aires Spanish uses 'vos' instead of 'tú', pronounces 'll/y' as 'sh'. Italian influence is heavy. Everyone calls everyone 'che'. Lunfardo slang is deeply embedded.

IN/Delhi.cultural_notes: Delhi mixes Hindi and Urdu freely — Hindustani street speech. Namaste/Namaskar with folded hands. Address elders with aap, not tu. English code-switching is normal among urban speakers. Write phrases in Devanagari with romanization.

slang_era.gen_z: yaar, scene on hai, full on, bhai, mast
slang_era.millennial: yaar, bilkul, chal, theek hai, bakwaas

IN/Mumbai.cultural_notes: Bambaiya Hindi is punchy and Marathi-tinged — 'apoon' for we, 'boss' for anyone. Extremely cosmopolitan; Marathi, Hindi, and English mix on the street. Direct and warm. Write phrases in Devanagari with romanization.

slang_era.gen_z: bhidu, jhakas, scene kya hai, full tight
slang_era.older: aap/ji forms, Marathi politeness borrowed into Hindi

ID/Jakarta.cultural_notes: Jakarta Indonesian drops formal endings and loves slang. 'Gue/lu' (I/you) is default among young people; 'saya/Anda' for formal. Smile-heavy, avoid blunt confrontation. Food and traffic are universal small talk. Latin script only.

ID/Bali.cultural_notes: Tourism-facing Indonesian with Balinese warmth underneath. Locals may switch to Balinese among themselves. Soft, hospitable tone. Respect temple etiquette (sarong, quiet). Latin script; keep teaching in Indonesian unless the user asks for Balinese.

TR/Istanbul.cultural_notes: Istanbul Turkish is the prestige standard. Hospitality is serious — tea offers are not optional. Use siz (formal you) with strangers and elders; sen with peers. Agglutinative morphology: teach whole usable phrases, not isolated stems. Latin script with Turkish letters (ğ, ş, ı, ç, ö, ü).

slang_era.gen_z: abi/abla, valla, süper, yok artık, tamam mı
slang_era.older: efendim, lütfen, teşekkür ederim, siz forms

PH/Manila.cultural_notes: Manila speech is Taglish — Tagalog and English weave mid-sentence naturally. Po/opo mark respect with elders. Warm, playful, face-saving humor. Teach Tagalog phrases but expect English mix; don't scold code-switching. Latin script.

slang_era.gen_z: bes, char, lodi, petmalu, sana all
slang_era.millennial: pare/mare, o sige, grabe, ang hirap

RU/Moscow.cultural_notes: Moscow Russian is the media standard. Blunt honesty is normal, not rude. Use вы with strangers; ты only when invited. Cases and aspect matter — teach whole phrases in context. Write phrases in Cyrillic with romanization.

slang_era.older: здравствуйте, пожалуйста, вы forms, fewer anglicisms

KE/Nairobi.cultural_notes: Nairobi mixes Kiswahili with Sheng (Swahili-English youth slang) and English. Greetings matter — Habari / Mambo before business. Warm and communal. Latin script. Teach standard Kiswahili phrases; note Sheng as street flavor, not the only register.

TZ/Dar es Salaam.cultural_notes: Dar Swahili is often treated as a prestige coastal variety — clearer, less Sheng than Nairobi. Greetings are elaborate and sincere. Respect elders; take time with hellos. Latin script. Prefer standard Kiswahili over Kenyan Sheng loans.

slang_era.gen_z: Mambo vipi, poa, fit, sawa tu
slang_era.older: shikamoo, marahaba, formal Salama / Habari za asubuhi
